verdict.rationale: Jitsu ships a first-party MCP server so an AI agent can manage the pipeline on the user's behalf: creating destinations, wiring streams, inspecting Live Events and editing Functions. That gives users an official path to operate the product through an agent. However, the natural-language layer comes from the user's external agent, not from Jitsu itself. missing for 10: a built-in natural-language command interface within Jitsu, hands-on or independent corroboration that agent-driven operation works reliably, documented examples of natural-language prompts or workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Jitsu runs an MCP server, so AI agents can manage your pipeline directly: create destinations, wire up streams, inspect Live Events, and edit Functions.
Point your AI agent at the Jitsu MCP server and it can configure your pipeline, watch Live Events in real time, and fix the Functions that transform your data
Point your agent at `https://use.jitsu.com/mcp`, approve it once in the browser, and it can run your data pipeline for you.
